newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen retreating on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen retreating on consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks are likely to continue consolidating on Monday on the lack of theme-backed market leaders and weak investor buying interest, brokers said.
Lagging customer deposits, seen as a gauge of investor confidence in the stock market, and a possibility of rising interest rates would further drag down the market, they said.
The composite stock index closed Saturday down 1.02 points to 730.43.
Brokers said the unclear future of the struggling Kia Group would also continue to haunt the market, although much of the bad news had already been reflected.

Friday's meeting of Kia's creditor banks failed to reach an agreement on detailing their earlier decision to bail out the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate. The creditors will meet again on Monday.
"The market is expected to further consolidate this week in the absence of any positive factors," said Koh Kyong-bae of Hyundai Securities.
Customer deposits were tallied at 3.01 trillion won as of August 1, down from 3.06 trillion on July 28, brokers said.
"Going below the three trillion won mark would significantly hurt sentiment," Koh said. -- JEAN YOON (822) 727 5643
